(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum) This appeal is filed by the
claimants questioning the quantum as well as the negligence on account of death of their unmarried
sister in the road traffic accident dated 15.4.2018.

The Tribunal in the absence of income proof assessed the income at Rs.3,000/- per month and deducting 50% towards personal expenses and applying multiplier 16 has awarded Rs.2,88,000/-
towards loss of dependency.
Tribunal in all awarded Rs.3,73,000/- with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

Tribunal while attributing negligence held that the driver of the goods vehicle in which the deceased was traveling was negligent to the tune of 70% and the driver of the parked goods vehicle was negligent to the tune of 30%.

sentences.text: The Tribunal having apportioned the negligence dismissed the claim petition against respondent No.4/New India Insurance company on the ground it is not liable to pay 70% of compensation since the inmates of the goods vehicle were traveling as gratuitous passengers.

The claim petition was in fact allowed against the owner of the offending truck i.e. respondent No.3 and 30% liability was fastened on respondents 1 and 2 primarily fixing the NC: 2024:KHC-K:9804 liability on respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants /claimants and the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Oriental Insurance Company as well as the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4/New India Assurance Company limited.
FINDING ON NEGLIGENCE:

5. This Court in MFA.No.202567/2019 considering the arguments advanced by the counsel appearing for the claimants and the counsel appearing for both the Insurance Companies has after meticulous examination of the material on record and on an elaborate discussion held that both the drivers of the truck were negligent and therefore, attributed negligence in the ratio of 50:50.
Accordingly, negligence is attributed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident.

Further more, since the truck bearing No. MH- 13-AX-2339 was used in violation of the policy conditions NC: 2024:KHC-K:9804 permitting 30 passengers to travel in the goods vehicle, Respondent No.3, who is the owner of the truck bearing No. MH-13-AX-2339 is liable to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.

Respondent No.2/Insurance Company who is the insurer of the goods vehicle bearing No. KA.36/A.2976 which was illegally parked is jointly and severally liable along with respondent No.1 to deposit 50% of the compensation awarded.
FINDING ON QUANTUM:
6. The claimants in the case on hand are the brothers of an unmarried sister who died in a road traffic accident dated 15.4.2012.
Admittedly, deceased was hardly aged 35 years and she was residing along with her brothers, who are the appellants herein.

Though the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company would vehemently argue and contend that claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act is not maintainable, this Court is not inclined to accede to the arguments advanced by the Insurance Company.

Equally, this Court is not NC: 2024:KHC-K:9804 inclined to accede to the arguments canvassed by the learned counsel appearing for the claimants that brothers though married were dependant on the income of the unmarried sister.

Having regard to the fact that deceased is an unmarried sister and that she was residing along with the claimants herein, this Court is of the view that compensation has to re-determined under the head of loss of estate and not under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, if the income is notionally assessed at Rs.6,000/- and if 40% is added towards future prospects, the income works out to Rs.8,400/-.
1/3rd of Rs.8,400/- has to be treated as the savings of the deceased, which works out to Rs.2,800/-.
By applying the multiplier of 16, compensation payable under the head of loss of estate works out to(Rs.2,800x12x16)= Rs.5,37,600/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court has also taken note of the fact that quantum determined by the Tribunal under the head of loss of dependency is not challenged by the Insurance Company.

Under conventional heads,
Rs.1,50,000/- is NC: 2024:KHC-K:9804 awarded.
Thus, total compensation re-determined by this Court works out to Rs.6,87,600/- as against Rs.3,73,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Thus,
claimants are held entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.3,14,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

8. For the foregoing reasons, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 19.12.2018 passed by the Tribunal in MVC.No.927/2012 is hereby modified.

(iii) The appellants/claimants are held entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.3,14,600/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
(iv) The negligence is fixed in the ratio of 50:50 on the drivers of both the vehicles.

Respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to deposit 50% of NC: 2024:KHC-K:9804 compensation awarded and balance 50% shall be paid by respondent No.3/Owner of the truck bearing No.
MH-13-AX-2339.
(v) The order of the Tribunal insofar as apportionment remains unaltered.

SD/-
